decision.detail: Sit up. Feet on the cold tile. I do not reach for the coat. I do not reach for the ticket. I reach for the envelope on the nightstand, the one I did not see until the radio gave me the third note and I turned my head and there it was, cream-colored, stamped, from Pittsburgh. I tear the seal. I pull out the receipt. I read the line. 'I know that voice. Play it again.' I read it again. I set the paper on the nightstand. I put my hands flat on the mattress. I stay sitting. I do not stand. I do not go to the window. I listen. The van backfires. I wait for the second one. It does not come. The radio plays a jingle for a tire shop. I fold the receipt back into the envelope. I put the envelope in my pocket. I stand up. I put on my shoes. I look at the ticket on the dresser. I do not pick it up yet. I look at my hands. I breathe. I pick up the ticket. I put on the coat. I walk to the door.
decision.intention: Read what arrived before I repeat what I already did. The voice line is new. It was not in the last three mornings. I will carry it to the coach and I will not call her tonight. I will sit in the terminal and I will think about whose voice she knows and why she wants to play it again, and I will get to her door at 7:30 with the question still in my pocket instead of a rehearsed sentence. The couch moves on Wednesday or it does not. I am not going to sleep on a bench and wake up here again with the same three lines and no answer. This time I carry the envelope. This time I do not reduce the day to a time and a door. I go, I arrive, I am a person at her door with a question, not a clock.

Pick an immediate physical act you can carry out, optional words and a practical intention. Your words do not make anyone else act. Silence is allowed. You may refuse, tell a lie, or leave without explaining yourself.
